title: Comparison inverse images of injective abelian sheaves are direct-image acyclic
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], with small sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and comparison geometric morphism $
u_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}	o X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Use its inverse image and direct image on abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For every injective abelian sheaf $I$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], the abelian sheaf $
u_X^{-1}I$ is acyclic for $
u_{X,*}$, meaning $$R^q
u_{X,*}(
u_X^{-1}I)=0\qquad(q>0).$$ Here $R^q
u_{X,*}$ is computed by an injective resolution in abelian pro-etale sheaves and degree-$q$ cohomology of its direct-image complex [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. No affineness, torsion, constructibility or finite coefficient ring hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 099V, label lemma-relative-comparison, proof first paragraph; affine input Tag 099U, label lemma-affine-vanishing

proof.text: Put $M=\nu_X^{-1}I$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf] to the continuous inclusion $u_X:X_{\mathrm{et}}\to X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For a fixed $q>0$ this identifies $R^q\nu_{X,*}M$ with the sheafification of $P(V)=H^q(u_X(V),M)$, where the latter is derived evaluation over the pro-etale object $V$. It suffices to show that $P$ is zero on affine etale objects and hence has zero sheafification. No direct-image evaluation is assumed exact.

source.place: Tag 099V, label lemma-relative-comparison, proof first paragraph

proof.text: Let $v:U\to X$ be an affine etale object. Set $J=v^{-1}_{\mathrm{et}}I$. The statement of [lem-sbc-etale-abelian-restriction-injectives] gives that $J$ is injective as an abelian sheaf on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. In particular, this is injectivity in precisely the coefficient category needed for affine vanishing, not injectivity in a finite-ring module category.

source.place: Tag 099V, label lemma-relative-comparison, proof first paragraph

proof.text: The slice over $U$ of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by clause (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]; etale $v$ is an object of the pro-etale site by the inclusion of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Under this identification $M|_U\cong\nu_U^{-1}J$. Here is the identification on sections and restrictions: for $t:T\to U$ weakly etale, [lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections] writes the two sides as $\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},(vt)^{-1}_{\mathrm{et}}I)$ and $\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},t^{-1}_{\mathrm{et}}v^{-1}_{\mathrm{et}}I)$. The composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] identifies these groups. The inverse-image functors preserve finite limits by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3). Naturality with the two projections from $I\times I$ makes the composition isomorphism for $I\times I$ the product of the two isomorphisms for $I$. Naturality with $+:I\times I\to I$ therefore says that the isomorphism preserves addition. Naturality with the zero map from the terminal sheaf and with $-:I\to I$ gives zero and negation compatibility. The same reasoning applies to the natural section formula of [lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections]. By the underlying-set convention in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3), these are exactly the abelian inverse images and their group laws. For an arrow $a:T'\to T$ over $U$, both restriction maps are section pullback followed by the composition identification. The associativity identity (2) and the unit identities (0)-(1) in the composition node make the two composites equal. Thus the objectwise maps form an isomorphism of abelian sheaves; they do not merely identify section sets.

source.place: Tag 099V, label lemma-relative-comparison, proof first paragraph

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization] to the abelian sheaf $M$ and the pro-etale object $U$. Combining it with the slice and coefficient identifications of step 3 gives $P(U)\cong H^q(U_{\mathrm{proet}},\nu_U^{-1}J)$. The scheme $U$ is affine, $J$ is injective in abelian etale sheaves by step 2, and $q>0$. Therefore [lem-cbc-abelian-affine-comparison-vanishing] makes this group zero. This proves vanishing for every affine etale object, even when $X$ is not affine.

source.place: Tag 099V, label lemma-relative-comparison, proof first paragraph

proof.text: Every etale object $V\to X$ has an affine open cover by [lem-pc-fppf-affine-open-cover]. The open inclusions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]; composing with $V\to X$ gives etale $X$-objects, as in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. Their joint surjectivity makes this a covering in [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Thus every element of $P(V)$ restricts to zero on a covering by affine objects. To conclude directly from the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], let $H$ be any abelian sheaf and $a:P\to H$ any presheaf morphism. For $s\in P(V)$ its image $a_V(s)$ restricts to zero on that cover; uniqueness in the sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] implies $a_V(s)=0$. Hence every such $a$ is zero. In particular the sheafification unit is zero, so its identity and zero endomorphisms have the same composite with the unit. The universal property forces them to be equal, proving $P^\#=0$. Step 1 now gives $R^q\nu_{X,*}(\nu_X^{-1}I)=0$. For the empty object every term of an injective resolution of $M$ has zero sections by the sheaf axiom for the empty cover, so its derived evaluation $P(\varnothing)$ is zero as well; no finite-cover or quasi-compactness hypothesis was used.
